title: Vision-based attention estimation and selection for social robot to perform natural interaction in the open world

quotes.text: In this paper, a novel vision system is proposed to estimate attention of people from rich visual clues for social robot to perform natural interactions with multiple participants in public environments.
We have conducted on-site experiments with the robot receptionist in various interaction scenarios.

fields.value: The paper presents a vision system that estimates each person's attention to a receptionist robot from multiple visual cues and combines them into an attention level. In an example with three people, the robot turned toward and greeted a person who looked, smiled, and spoke to it; the estimated attention fell when he turned to talk with another person.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ3; RQ4; RQ5 — The paper operationalizes human attention through visual cues, shows how the estimate supports selecting and facing a person in a multiparty scene, and describes an observed attention-level change. It also reports the vision implementation and identifies the receptionist robot platform; it does not explain how embodiment influenced the study.
